newsitem.title: UK: LME base metals drift off highs in light volumes.
newsitem.headline: LME base metals drift off highs in light volumes.

text.p: The base metals ran out of steam at the highs on Monday and drifted back by the end of the afternoon trading session amid light volumes despite Third Wednesday pricing.
Flagship copper made a push to the upside in the afternoon, but prices failed to breach tough support at $2,490.
Three months metals touched $2,487 per tonne, just $1 off Friday's 11-1/2 month high, and then turned back.
Prices eventually settled $8 firmer at $2,474 per tonne, with the cash to threes backwardation steady at around $70.
"Volumes are quite light, with most of Europe on holiday, and the buying ran out in the afternoon," a trader said.
"People may also be waiting for fresh news out of South American supplies before getting too excited," a trader said.
Nickel dazzled early on with an advance to the highest in nearly two months after breaching resistance at $7,900.
But profit taking reversed the trend and nickel shed most of its gains by the close, ending just $35 firmer at $7,855.
"The volumes weren't there," a trader noted. "By the end of the kerb it was down sharply."
Zinc fell by $6 to $1,342 following a whopping 12,200-tonne LME stock drawdown which mystified some in the market.

It was unclear what was behind the stock build at the St. Louis LME warehouse, with some traders believing the metal was of South American origin and others saying it was European metal shipped out five weeks ago.

Lead dipped following by news that a potential disruption to North American supply was averted when workers at Exide Corp's Reading secondary lead smelter in Pennsylvania returned to work on Monday, ending a strike started last week.
The company said battery making and distribution at the the 90,000-short ton per year plant were unaffected by the dispute.
Tin was very quiet, keeping to a tiny $15 trading range all day. It ended virtually unchanged at $5,750/60, compared to to $5,760.
Alloy was indicated softer at $1,505/10, versus $1,517 previously.
